description: This is a police request. Police enforces policy, so an egress request must name its target: either a provider or a destination app and component.

anonymization.description: How to anonymize the data. If deanonymize is true, then VariablSize is required.
anonymization.title: anonymization

conversationID.description: Identifies the conversation this request belongs to. Apex records it on the resulting log, which is what groups the successive requests of one conversation together in the logs and in the conversation view, and it is also made available to the analyzers and to policies. Send the same value on every request of the same conversation.
conversationID.title: conversationID

destination.description: The destination for this request. When destination app and component are set, they become the policy target and the provider field must not be set. When an egress request names neither a provider nor a destination app and component, the provider is resolved from the destination host, and then from the model. On the police API an egress request must end up with a target: the policy needs one. On the scan API it may end up with none to run a plain scan that targets nothing, in which case the app component identified by the caller's token is reported as the destination so that the request still shows up in traces.
destination.title: destination

direction.description: The direction of the traffic for this request, relative to the app component the caller's token identifies. Determines whether the ingress or the egress policies of that app component are evaluated.
direction.title: direction

encryptionEgress.description: The encryption details of the connection from the app component to the origin server, if known. When it is set, encryptionEgressState defaults to Encrypted.
encryptionEgress.title: encryptionEgress

encryptionEgressState.description: Whether the connection from the app component to the origin server was encrypted. Unknown when it is not known. When left Unknown and encryptionEgress is set, it is considered Encrypted. It must not be Unencrypted when encryptionEgress is set.
encryptionEgressState.title: encryptionEgressState

encryptionIngress.description: The encryption details of the connection from the client to the app component, if known. When it is set, encryptionIngressState defaults to Encrypted.
encryptionIngress.title: encryptionIngress

encryptionIngressState.description: Whether the connection from the client to the app component was encrypted. Unknown when it is not known. When left Unknown and encryptionIngress is set, it is considered Encrypted. It must not be Unencrypted when encryptionIngress is set.
encryptionIngressState.title: encryptionIngressState

messages.description: Messages to process and provide detections for. Use data in extractions for processing binary data.
messages.title: messages

model.description: The model used by the request. When the request names neither a provider nor a destination app and component and the destination host resolves no provider either, the provider serving this model becomes the policy target.
model.title: model

provider.description: The name of the provider to use for policy resolutions. Must not be set when destination app and component are set. When neither this nor the destination app and component are set on an egress request, the provider is resolved from the destination host, and then from the model. On the police API an egress request must end up with a target. On the scan API it may end up with none to run a plain scan that targets nothing.
provider.title: provider

source.description: The source of this request. Optional: on egress the source is already known from the caller's token, and on ingress it can be left out for an anonymous external caller.
source.title: source

tools.description: The various tools used by the request.
tools.title: tools

trace.description: The trace context this request belongs to. When it is set, Apex places the span it creates for this request inside your trace instead of starting a new one, and setting it enables tracing for this request even when the application is otherwise configured not to trace. What Apex actually recorded is reported back in the 'trace' field of the response.
trace.title: trace

title: PoliceRequest
